sources.title: From flint to stainless steel: Observations on surgical instrument composition
sources.authorsRaw: John Kirkup
summary: traces what surgical tools have been made of from stone age (flint) to modern age (disposable plastics)
argues first instruments were substitutes for fingers and teeth and were made to pull out thorns and arrowheads
tools were primarily made from animal, plant, and minerals before metal became the standard
the material to make the tools have always followed whatever technology existed at the time
says heat sterilization is a turning point that forced a change in what tools could be made of
sources.apaRaw: Kirkup J. (1993). From flint to stainless steel: observations on surgical instrument composition. Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England, 75(5), 365–374.

sources.title: Ignaz Semmelweis and the birth of infection control
sources.authorsRaw: Mark Best and Duncan Neuhauser
summary: history of Vienna doctor that figured out that doctors' unwashed hands were killing new mothers
Semmelweis was the first helth worker to prove by experiment that handwashing prevents infection
His 1861 book explained that the finding was poorly written and dismissed by other doctors
died in a public insane asylum at 47 (5 years after publishing his book)
sources.apaRaw: Best, M., & Neuhauser, D. (2004). Ignaz Semmelweis and the birth of infection control. Quality & safety in health care, 13(3), 233–234. https://doi.org/10.1136/qhc.13.3.233

sources.title: Slow Ideas: Some innovations spread fast. How do you speed the ones that don't?
sources.authorsRaw: Atul Gawande
summary: asks why anesthesia caught on almost overnight in 1846 while antiseptic surgery took decades
anesthesia was standard in most American and European hospitals in 7 years; Lister published in The Lancet in 1867 and was ignored
Says that the reason for the time difference was due to pain being immediate and germs being delayed
anesthesia made surgeon's job easier, while Lister's made surgeons spray acid that burned their hands
later in the article applies same logic to the spread of safer childbirth practices in India
sources.apaRaw: Atul Gawande. (2013, July 22). Sharing slow ideas. The New Yorker. The New Yorker. https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2013/07/29/slow-ideas

sources.title: Marvellous Medical Materials: Stainless Steel - Part One
sources.authorsRaw: Institute of Making, University College London
summary: explains why heat sterilization forced a complete redesign of surgical tools
steam killed germs but also destroyed wood, ivory, and handles tools used to have
all-metal instruments became the new norm as a result
heat also sped up rusting, so tools were plated with nickel and chrome to counteract it
stainless steel replaced it between 1913-1925
sources.apaRaw: Institute of Making. (2017). Marvellous medical materials: Stainless Steel - part one - institute of making. Institute of Making. https://www.instituteofmaking.org.uk/blog/marvellous-medical-material-stainless-steel-part-one

sources.title: Charles W. Hull - 3D printing (stereolithography)
sources.authorsRaw: European Patent Office
summary: Short video on the man that invented 3D printing, was made for European Inventor Award
covers stereolithography, original method that hardened liquid resin with UV light
3D printing originated between 1983-1986
Shows the ancestor of the melted-filament method
sources.apaRaw: European Patent Office. (2014, May 6). Charles W. Hull - 3D printing (stereolithography) [YouTube Video]. In YouTube. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3uYsviZ8Cuo

sources.title: Origins: 3D Printing
sources.authorsRaw: Trent Knoss
summary: tells story of night in 1983 when Hull printed first object ever made using 3D printing
first object was a small plastic cup, wife's reaction was disbelief
built idea on nights and weekends in a borrowed lab after > 1 yearof work
saw it as a protyping tool, not medical technology
sources.apaRaw: Knoss, T. (2016, June). Origins: 3D printing. University of Colorado Boulder. Alumni Association. https://www.colorado.edu/coloradan/2016/06/01/origins-3d-printing

sources.title: Surgery and global health: A view from beyond the OR
sources.authorsRaw: Paul E. Farmer and Jim Y. Kim
summary: named surgery the "neglected stepchild" of global public health
Africa has fewer doctors per person than any other continent, surgeons are even rarer
nearly all surgeons work in cities, while majority of population is rural
poor countries surgery is mostly available to those that can pay out of pocket
no global fund for surgery unlike AIDS, TB, and malaria
sources.apaRaw: Farmer, P. E., & Kim, J. Y. (2008). Surgery and global health: a view from beyond the OR. World journal of surgery, 32(4), 533–536. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00268-008-9525-9

sources.title: Medical Applications for 3D printing: Current and projected uses
sources.authorsRaw: Lee Ventola
summary: snapshot of what medical 3D printing looked like in 2014 before it's popularity rose
sorts uses into 3 groups, making tissues and organs, making prosthetics implants and models, and drug research
explains main printing methods used in medicine
shows how recently printed surgical tools became a serious idea
sources.apaRaw: Ventola C. L. (2014). Medical Applications for 3D Printing: Current and Projected Uses. P & T : a peer-reviewed journal for formulary management, 39(10), 704–711.

sources.title: Additively manufactured medical products -- the FDA perspective
sources.authorsRaw: Matthew Di Prima, James Coburn, David Hwang, Jennifer Kelly, Akm Khairuzzaman, Laura Ricles
summary: written by FDA staff on how the FDA decides wheter a printed medical product is safe to sell
documents the point where printed devices stopped being experimental
says a 3D printed drug has already hit the market
says FDA's job is to allow new tech without letting unsafe ones through
sources.apaRaw: Di Prima, M., Coburn, J., Hwang, D., Kelly, J., Khairuzzaman, A., & Ricles, L. (2016). Additively manufactured medical products – the FDA perspective. 3D Printing in Medicine, 2(1). https://doi.org/10.1186/s41205-016-0005-9

sources.title: A critical review of initial 3D printed products responding to COVID-19 health and supply chain challenges
sources.authorsRaw: James I. Novak, Jennifer Loy
summary: documents what happened when hospitals ran out of supplies and people started printing replacements
collected data on 91 printing projetcts that started before April 1, 2020
60% projects were on protective equipment, of that 60%, 62% were face shields
melted-filament method common on hobby printers, was most used tech
most projects shared designs through websites instead of official methods
sources.apaRaw: Novak, J. I., & Loy, J. (2020). A critical review of initial 3D printed products responding to COVID-19 health and supply chain challenges. Emerald Open Research, 2, 24. https://doi.org/10.35241/emeraldopenres.13697.1

sources.title: 3D printing surgical instruments: Are we there yet?
sources.authorsRaw: Timothy M. Rankin, Nicholas A. Giovinco, Daniel J. Cucher, George Watts, Bonnie Hurwitz, and David G. Armstrong
summary: replicated Army/Navy reactor from PLA on an FDM (fused deposition modeling) printer; took 90 mins per print
printed tools were able to withstand 13.6 kg of force before breaking
force tolerance was same before and after sterilzation
freshly printed PLA was sterile, no PCR product when tested for traces of bacteria
each retractor (printed object) weighed 16g and used $0.46 of PLA
sources.apaRaw: Rankin, T. M., Giovinco, N. A., Cucher, D. J., Watts, G., Hurwitz, B., & Armstrong, D. G. (2014). Three-dimensional printing surgical instruments: Are we there yet? Journal of Surgical Research, 189(2), 193–197. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jss.2014.02.020

sources.title: Global burden of surgical disease: An estimation from the provider perspective
sources.authorsRaw: Mark G. Shirme, Stephen W. Bickler, Blake C. Alkire, and Charlie Mock
summary: surveyed 173 surgical and non-surgical providers from 4 regions across the world
asked what percent of patients each with one of 21 diseases would need a surgeon
providers estimated surgery is needed for 28-32% of the global population facing the burden of a disease
non-surgeons estimated 25-30% would need it, surgeons estimated 30-35%
sources.apaRaw: Shrime, M. G., Bickler, S. W., Alkire, B. C., & Mock, C. (2015). Global burden of surgical disease: An estimation from the provider perspective. The Lancet Global Health, 3(Special Issue 2), S8–S9. https://doi.org/10.1016/s2214-109x(14)70384-5

sources.title: Applications of PLA in modern medicine
sources.authorsRaw: Vincent DeStefano, Salaar Khan, and Alonzo Tabada
summary: DeStefano et al. looked at PLA in tissue engineering, implants, drug delivery, orthopedics, and medical tools
They saw that PLA is renewable, biodegradable, and easy to synthesize; however, they also saw that its properties could be changed using crystallinity and additives
They analyzed the PLA and saw that the degradation of PLA depends on its geometry, molecular weight, crystallinity, sterilization, and mechanical stress
They saw that, in a lab testing environment, PLA blood vessel grafts loss 0.77% mass in 25 days and 1.93% in 50 days, however they were still able to retain some structural integrity
sources.apaRaw: DeStefano, V., Khan, S., & Tabada, A. (2020). Applications of PLA in modern medicine. Engineered Regeneration, 1(1), 76–87. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engreg.2020.08.002

sources.title: 3D printed PLA Army-Navy retractors when used as linear retractors yield clinically acceptable tolerances
sources.authorsRaw: Joshua V. Chen, Alexis B. C. Dang, Carlin S. Lee, and Alan B. C. Dang
summary: printed the same retractor model repeatedly while changing printer settings, then pulled on each one until it broke
surgeons set 35 N as the hardest a retractor should ever be pulled; the best 3D printed model was able to 15x more
best settings was 30% infill, 3 outer wall alyers, a triangle pattern inside, and thicker joints
identical spools from the same brand made retractors that had noticeably different strength
the strongest version they made costed $1.25
sources.apaRaw: Chen, J. V., Dang, A. B. C., Lee, C. S., & Dang, A. B. C. (2019). 3D printed PLA Army-Navy retractors when used as linear retractors yield clinically acceptable tolerances. 3D Printing in Medicine, 5(1), 16. PubMed Central. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41205-019-0053-z

sources.title: Identifying a commerically-available 3D printing process that minimizes model distortion after annealing and autoclaving and the effect of steam sterilization on mechanical strength
sources.authorsRaw: Joshua V. Chen, Kara S. Tanaka, Alan B. C. Dang, Alexis Dang
summary: printed test cubes using 7 different plastics and 4 inner patterns, measured each one before and after heating and sterilizing
"annealing" means baking or boiling a printed part to make it stronger; used 100 celsius water bath for 30 mins
sterilizing in steam autoclave at 134 celsius ruined strength; retractors went from 95 N -> 15.7 N
annealing first raised strength to 127.3 N but sterlizing caused it to drop to 19.8 N
only redisned, thicker retractor was able to survive both annealing and sterilziing, broke at 164.8 N
sources.apaRaw: Chen, J. V., Tanaka, K. S., Dang, A. B. C., & Dang, A. (2020). Identifying a commercially-available 3D printing process that minimizes model distortion after annealing and autoclaving and the effect of steam sterilization on mechanical strength. 3D printing in medicine, 6(1), 9. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41205-020-00062-9

sources.title: Effects of Sterilization on the dimensional and mechanical behavior of polylactic acid pieces produced by fused deposition modeling
sources.authorsRaw: Israel Garnica-Bohórquez, Viviana R. Güiza-Argüello, Clara I. López-Gualdrón
summary: compared 2 affordable ways hospitals sterilize equipment: steam and formaldehyde gas
used actual procedure from a public hospital in Colombia instead of idealized lab procedure
tested plain printed PLA bars, not finished instruments
checked wheter the piecese changed shape and wheter they got weaker
aimed at low-cost tools like surgical guides and anatomical models
sources.apaRaw: Garnica-Bohórquez, I., Güiza-Argüello, V. R., & López-Gualdrón, C. I. (2023). Effect of Sterilization on the Dimensional and Mechanical Behavior of Polylactic Acid Pieces Produced by Fused Deposition Modeling. Polymers, 15(15), 3317. https://doi.org/10.3390/polym15153317

sources.title: Bacterial biofilm formation on nano-copper added PLA suited for 3D printed face masks
sources.authorsRaw: Annika Kiel, Bernhard peter Kaltschmidt, EhsanAsghari, Andreas Hütten, Barbara Kaltschmidt, Christian Kaltschmidt
summary: compared a filament sold as germ-killing (had cooper) aginst regular PLA
grew 3 common hospital bacteria on both and counted the colonies that survived
bacteria stuck to and grew on every material tested, including the "germ-killing" filament
copper only slowed down 1 bacteria
this paper suggests that filaments sold as antibacterial may not necessarily protect against a lot
sources.apaRaw: Kiel, A., Kaltschmidt, B. P., Asghari, E., Hütten, A., Kaltschmidt, B., & Kaltschmidt, C. (2022). Bacterial Biofilm Formation on Nano-Copper Added PLA Suited for 3D Printed Face Masks. Microorganisms, 10(2), 439. https://doi.org/10.3390/microorganisms10020439

sources.title: Sustainable thermal post-processing of PLA 3D prints: Increased dimensional precdision and autoclave compatibility
sources.authorsRaw: Florina Chiscop, Carmen-Cristiana Cazacu, Dragos-Alexandru Cazacu, Costel Emil Cotet
summary: packed printed PLA parts in either table salt or silicone rubber, then baked them so that they couldn't warp
silicone worked better: parts stayed within 0.5% of their original side, salt shrank them ~2%
untreated PLA started sagging at 70 celsius, no where near stelizing temps
packed parts stayed rigid up to 130 celsius for thin pieces and 175 celsius for solid ones
real surgical part still fit and worked after an hour of steam sterilizing at 134 celsius
sources.apaRaw: Chiscop, F., Cazacu, C. C., Cazacu, D. A., & Cotet, C. E. (2025). Sustainable Thermal Post-Processing of PLA 3D Prints: Increased Dimensional Precision and Autoclave Compatibility. Journal of functional biomaterials, 16(9), 334. https://doi.org/10.3390/jfb16090334

sources.title: The effect of steam sterilization on different 3D printable materials for surgical use in veterinary medicine
sources.authorsRaw: Phillipp Dautzenberg, Holger A. volk, Nikolaus Huels, Lena Cieciora, Katharina Dohmen, Matthias Lüpke, Herman Seifert, Oliver Harms
summary: compared Pla against 4 other printing plastics using standard hospital steam cycle: 20 mins at 121 celsius
printed each plastic hollow (30% infill) and solid to see if density mattered
every plastic came out of sterilizer slightly warped or shrunken
plastic called GreenTEC Pro held its shape best and looked most usable for surgery
authors noted that nobody has tested yet if these parts are actually germ-free or strong enough to use
sources.apaRaw: Dautzenberg, P., Volk, H. A., Huels, N., Cieciora, L., Dohmen, K., Lüpke, M., Seifert, H., & Harms, O. (2021). The effect of steam sterilization on different 3D printable materials for surgical use in veterinary medicine. BMC veterinary research, 17(1), 389. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12917-021-03065-8

sources.title: Effects of Sterilization Methods on Different 3D printable Materials for Templates of Physician-Modified Aortic Stent Grafts Used in Vascular Surgery -- A Preliminary Study
sources.authorsRaw: Paweł Rynio, Katarzyna Galant, Łukasz Wójcik, Bartłomiej Grygorcewicz, Arkadiusz Kazimierczak, Aleksander Falkowski, Piotr Gutowski, Barbara Dołęgowska, Miłosz Kawa
summary: printed same surgical template in 6 plastics (PLA included)
deliberately coated them in bacteria and tried 4 different sterilization methods
all methods killed bacteria completely, plastic type didn't matter
although all killed bacteria, the shape was compromised: steam at 121 celsius badly warped PLA, while gentler methods left every other plastic fine
type of plastic is the real factor on if a tool survives the heat
sources.apaRaw: Rynio, P., Galant, K., Wójcik, Ł., Grygorcewicz, B., Kazimierczak, A., Falkowski, A., Gutowski, P., Dołęgowska, B., & Kawa, M. (2022). Effects of Sterilization Methods on Different 3D Printable Materials for Templates of Physician-Modified Aortic Stent Grafts Used in Vascular Surgery-A Preliminary Study. International journal of molecular sciences, 23(7), 3539. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms23073539

sources.title: The effect of chemical cleaning on mechanical properties of three-dimensional printed polylactic acid
sources.authorsRaw: Julie Fleischer, Jan-Carel Diehl, Linda Wauben, Jenny Dankelman
summary: tested whether repeated chemical cleaning weakens 3D printed PLA, aimed at hospitals in low and middle income countries
printed pulling test samples at 6 different printer settings, then soaked them in Cidex OPA or a chlorine solution
used 2 exposure patterns: 7 days straight, or 25 short cycles
weighed every sample before and after, then pulled them apart; a third of the treatments gained weight, up to 8.3%, but the samples with the smoothest surfaces did not change
strength moved in both directions: median increase of 12.5%, largest decrease of 8.8%
warns that surface pores must be kept small so soaked-in disinfectant does not transfer to people
sources.apaRaw: Fleischer, J., Diehl, J.-C., Wauben, L., & Dankelman, J. (2020). The effect of chemical cleaning on mechanical properties of three-dimensional printed polylactic acid. Journal of Medical Devices, 14(1), Article 011109. https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4046120

sources.title: Polylactic acid as a suitable material for 3D printing of protective masks in times of COVID-19 pandemic
sources.authorsRaw: Eva Vaňková, Petra Kašparová, Josef Khun, Anna Machková, Jaroslav Julák, Michal Sláma, Jan Hodek, Lucie Ulrychová, Jan Weber, Klára Obrová, Karin Kosulin, Thomas Lion, Vladimír Scholtz
summary: checked whether 3D printed PLA can be cleaned and reused, and whether the plastic survives the cleaning
contaminated 1 cm squares of printed PLA with E. coli, a skin bacteria, and a yeast, then soaked them for 15 minutes in 96% ethanol, 70% isopropanol, or bleach
all 3 disinfectants completely removed the bacteria and the yeast
5 rounds of 15 minute isopropanol slightly melted the plastic and shrank the gaps between printed lines from about 6 micrometers down to 3.3-4, but the surface itself stayed undamaged
masks actually worn for 4 hours dropped from an average of about 2,455 colonies to 7 after 15 minutes in ethanol
microscope images showed the pores were closed deeper inside the part, and no test particles passed through
sources.apaRaw: Vaňková, E., Kašparová, P., Khun, J., Machková, A., Julák, J., Sláma, M., Hodek, J., Ulrychová, L., Weber, J., Obrová, K., Kosulin, K., Lion, T., & Scholtz, V. (2020). Polylactic acid as a suitable material for 3D printing of protective masks in times of COVID-19 pandemic. PeerJ, 8, e10259. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.10259

sources.title: Effects of autoclaving and disinfection on 3D surgical guides using LCD technology for dental implant
sources.authorsRaw: Badreddine Labakoum, Amr Farhan, Lhoucine Ben Taleb, Azeddine Mouhsen, Aissam Lyazidi
summary: compared 3 ways of treating 3D printed dental surgical guides: autoclave at 121 celsius, autoclave at 134 celsius, and 20 minutes in 70% isopropyl alcohol
made 100 samples total, with an untreated control group for comparison
used a 3 point bending test following ASTM D790, the standard for flexural strength of plastic bars
both autoclave temperatures changed the shape and the mechanical behavior of the guides
the alcohol group came out closest to the untreated control in both shape and strength, so the authors recommended alcohol over heat
important limit: these were resin printed on an LCD printer, not PLA on a filament printer
sources.apaRaw: Labakoum, B., Farhan, A., Taleb, L. B., Mouhsen, A., & Lyazidi, A. (2024). Effects of autoclaving and disinfection on 3D surgical guides using LCD technology for dental implant. 3D Printing in Medicine, 10(1), 14. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41205-024-00214-1

sources.title: Investigation of the effect of exposure to liquid chemicals on the strength performance of 3D-printed parts from different filament types
sources.authorsRaw: Arslan Kaptan
summary: soaked test bars of 8 different filament plastics in 8 chemicals, including isopropyl alcohol at both 75% and 99%, then pulled and struck them to see what strength was left
followed ASTM D638 for pulling and ASTM D256 for impact, with 3 samples per combination
PLA was one of the 2 weakest plastics against alcohol; after 7 days in 99% isopropyl alcohol it kept only about 60-70% of its pulling strength and 55-60% of its impact strength
PLA lost almost nothing in plain water, so the damage comes from the alcohol and not from simply being wet
samples were fully submerged for 1 hour, 24 hours, or 7 days, which is harsher than wiping a tool and letting it dry
sources.apaRaw: Kaptan, A. (2025). Investigation of the effect of exposure to liquid chemicals on the strength performance of 3D-printed parts from different filament types. Polymers, 17(12), 1637. https://doi.org/10.3390/polym17121637

sources.title: Antibacterial drug-release polydimethylsiloxane coating for 3D-printing dental polymer: Surface alterations and antimicrobial effects
sources.authorsRaw: Hang-Nga Mai, Dong Choon Hyun, Ju Hayng Park, Do-Yeon Kim, Sang Min Lee, Du-Hyeong Lee
summary: explains why 3D printed plastic holds onto bacteria: tiny pores form when air gets trapped between layers or when layers do not fuse completely
coated half of 60 printed disks with a silicone based layer carrying an antiseptic, and left the other half bare
the coating filled in the polishing scratches and the printing pores, measurably smoothing the surface and making it more water repelling
bacteria counts dropped from about 211 to 71 units on the coated disks
argues a coating is a way to reduce bacteria without changing the mechanical properties of the part underneath
limits: dental resin printing rather than PLA, and the coating released an antiseptic drug rather than acting as a plain sealant
sources.apaRaw: Mai, H.-N., Hyun, D. C., Park, J. H., Kim, D.-Y., Lee, S. M., & Lee, D.-H. (2020). Antibacterial drug-release polydimethylsiloxane coating for 3D-printing dental polymer: Surface alterations and antimicrobial effects. Pharmaceuticals, 13(10), 304. https://doi.org/10.3390/ph13100304

sources.title: Experimental study on mechanical properties of FDM 3D printed polylactic acid fabricated parts using response surface methodology
sources.authorsRaw: Shashwath Patil, T. Sathish, Emad Makki, Jayant Giri
summary: this study how changing 3 print settings could impact the strength of PLA strength, they changed layer height, part orientation, and infill density
they printed the pieces on a Creality ender-3, open-source hobby printer, using 1.75 mm filament
the pieces used to measure tensile strength used ASTM D638 and pieces measured for bending ability used ASTM D790
they used the Box-Behnken design to plan 17 experimental runs instead of testing every combo to save time and resources
the best tensile strength they got was: 0.2 mm layer height, 60 degree orientation, 80% infill, at 14.48 MPa
sources.apaRaw: Patil, S., Sathish, T., Makki, E., & Giri, J. (2024). Experimental study on mechanical properties of FDM 3D printed polylactic acid fabricated parts using response surface methodology. AIP Advances, 14(3). https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0191017

sources.title: Mechanical Properties of Components Fabricated with Open-Source 3-D Printers Under Realistic Environmental Conditions
summary: measured part strength from hobby printers in ordinary conditions, to stimulate what it would be like in a realistic scenario
showed that hobby-printers can produce results that can be reported and analyzed properly
sources.apaRaw: Tymrak, B. M., Kreiger, M., & Pearce, J. M. (2014). Mechanical properties of components fabricated with open-source 3-D printers under realistic environmental conditions. Materials & Design, 58(1), 242–246. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matdes.2014.02.038

sources.title: How to optimize the drop plate method for enumerating bacteria
sources.authorsRaw: Becky Herigstad, Martin Hamilton, Joanna Heersink
summary: used a reference paper for counting live bacteria and dropped small measured volumes of bacteria onto agar plates
this drop plating method takes less time than letting the colonies, and colonies might actually be easier to count accurately
However, there is no standardized way to do this method: some people have used 10x dilutions while others have used 2x
their method also calculates how starting volume, dilution factor, and drop size could affect any error in their count of bacteria colonies
sources.apaRaw: Herigstad, B., Hamilton, M., & Heersink, J. (2001). How to optimize the drop plate method for enumerating bacteria. Journal of microbiological methods, 44(2), 121–129. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0167-7012(00)00241-4

sources.title: Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities, 2008 (updated June 2024)
sources.authorsRaw: William A. Rutala, David J. Weber, and the Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee
summary: this is a set of guidelines published by the CDC that determines what level of cleaning a medical device actually requires in healthcare facilities
the CDC says that anything entering sterile tissue must be sterile
they also said that steam is the preferred sterilization method
these guidelines prioritized cleaning tools first, since sterilization fails if organic material is still on the surface of a tool
sources.apaRaw: CDC, Rutala, W., Weber, D., & Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee. (2024, May 21). Disinfection and sterilization guideline. Infection Control. https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/disinfection-and-sterilization/index.html

sources.title: TESTING 3D printed INFILL PATTERNS for their STRENGTH
sources.authorsRaw: Stefan Hermann, CNC Kitchen
summary: this youtuber crushed 22mm printed cubes to compare 8 infill patterns on a modified tensile machine
every cube used identical walls so the same design of pieces could be crushed from the top and from the side, so that the only thing that changes is the type of filament or method used
they weighed a test batch first and adjusted infill percentages so that all samples used same amount of plastic to get rid of some confounding variables
rectilinear design held 309 kg in the direction of how tools are printed (bottom->top) but only 191 kg from the side, about 40% weaker from the sides than from the top or bottom
grid, triangle line, and honeycomb exceeded machine's limit of 3.5kN so they can't be accurately measured
sources.apaRaw: CNC Kitchen. (2018, July 27). TESTING 3D printed infill patterns for their STRENGTH [YouTube Video]. In YouTube. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=upELI0HmzHc

sources.title: Serial Dilutions and Plating: Microbial Enumeration
sources.authorsRaw: JoVE Science Education
summary: they serial diluted a sample 10x at a time, meaning that 1mL into 9mL of sterile saline, and continued that across 10 tubes
the scientist then spread 100 microliters of chosen dilutions on agar and counted the colonies that grow
they didn't account plates that had less than 30 colonies or more than 300, as they counted it as outliers and ignored that data
CFU/mL = average colonies x dilution factor / volume plated
they showed streak plating and separated the bacterial colonies by appearance instead of counting
sources.apaRaw: JoVE Science Education Database. (2024). Serial dilutions and plating: Microbial enumeration | protocol. Www.Jove.Com. https://www.jove.com/v/10507/serial-dilutions-and-plating-microbial-enumeration

sources.title: Serial Dilutions and Plate Counts
sources.authorsRaw: Bio-Rad Laboratories
summary: they diluted it 10x at a time, 100 microliters of a culture into 900 microliters of a culture of LB Broth, and spread it across 7 test tubes
they mixed the test tubes using vortexing and pipetting up and down at least 5 times between each step
the scientist then spread the bacteria culture on the whole surface of an agar plate, includin the edge and repeated it for each dilution
the agar plates where then stacked upside down and incubated at 37 celsius for 16-24 hours
sources.apaRaw: Bio-Rad Laboratories. (2012, October 16). Serial dilution and plate counts [Video recording]. In YouTube. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pmRUBYlPMBM

sources.title: How to improve your 3D prints with annealing
sources.authorsRaw: Jakub Kočí, Prusa Research
summary: tested annealing across large batch of small prism samples using temps from 70 celsius all the way up to 170 celsius
hotter temps meant stronger layer bonding, but past a point parts shrunk, twisted, and softened
Even at the lowest temp (70 celsius) parts didn't come out same size as they went in
sources.apaRaw: Kočí, J. (2019, December 6). How to improve your 3D prints with annealing. Original Prusa 3D Printers. https://blog.prusa3d.com/how-to-improve-your-3d-prints-with-annealing_31088/

sources.title: Low Cost Unviersal Tensile Testing Machine
sources.authorsRaw: Xieshi Zhang, Hackaday.io project
summary: Zhang tested a ~$300 tensile tester built from printed and common store parts, against $12,900+ commercian one
it handled loads under 1000 N and can run compression tests as well as tension
he argued that rapid-prototyping work doesn't need commercial machine level precision all the time
sources.apaRaw: Zhang, X. (2023). Low cost universal tensile testing machine. Hackaday.Io. https://hackaday.io/project/192166-low-cost-universal-tensile-testing-machine

sources.title: Annealing PLA Prints: What It Does and Doesn't
sources.authorsRaw: Stefan Hermann, CNC Kitchen
summary: Hermann annealed the test pieces at 100 celsius for 45 minutes in a preheated oven, then slowly cooled the pieces by
after cooling, he saw that tensile strength rose from 63.5 Mpa to 68.2 Mpa meaning that it had a 7.5% increase, although it is important, it isn't really that big
however, layer adhesion didn't move at all (42kg before + after), meaning heat treatment doesn't fuse layers
the printed piece warping reached 10%, shrinking in X and Y, growing in Z, percentage varied too much to correct with scaling
leaving the parts on build plate with supports attached reduced warping
however, burying parts in sand didn't help the warping issue
sources.apaRaw: Hermann, S., & CNC Kitchen. (2019, September 25). CNC kitchen. CNC Kitchen. https://www.cnckitchen.com/blog/better-performing-3d-prints-with-annealing-but-part-1-pla

sources.title: Infiltration-assisted mechanical strengthening of 3D-printed polypropylene lattice and thin-walled tube structures
sources.authorsRaw: Hakkı Özer
summary: method for pushing epoxy into the hidden gaps inside a 3D print instead of only painting the outside
dipped printed parts into epoxy inside an ultrasonic bath for about 120 seconds, at 4 different epoxy thicknesses
weighed every part before and after on a balance reading to 0.0001 g, and used the weight gain to estimate how much of the inside got filled
thick epoxy sat on the outside as a shell up to 193 micrometers and barely got in; thin epoxy soaked in but left almost no surface layer; medium thickness was the balance
shows that weight gain alone can be misleading, because it does not say whether the epoxy went inside or just built up on the surface
limits: tested on polypropylene rather than PLA, and aimed at crash strength rather than cleaning
sources.apaRaw: Özer, H. (2025). Infiltration-assisted mechanical strengthening of 3D-printed polypropylene lattice and thin-walled tube structures. Polymers, 17(19), 2604. https://doi.org/10.3390/polym17192604

sources.title: Reuse of catheters and devices labelled for single use: evidence, recommendations and oversight
sources.authorsRaw: Thomas C. Crawford, Kim A Eagle
summary: argues reusing single use tools can be ethically justified when new devices aren't affordable in a country
Safe reuse gives poorer patients that can't afford highest quality care a real chance at some level of care
sets conditions, reuse must be transparent and devices must work about as well as new ones
says most safety studies backing reuse are decades old and vary widely in their qualities

sources.authorsRaw: Yamirot Merga Duffa, Zerihun Shimelis Kasa, Kibrewossen Kiflu Aklilu, Feyissa Regassa Senbato, Zelalem Tazu Bonger, Eyasu Tigabu Seyoum, Eden Dagnachew Zeleke, Leulseged Takele Chekol, Zelalem Mekuria, Samuel Muluye Welelaw, Joan-Miquel Balada-Llasat, Shu-Hua Wang & Tadesse Eguale
summary: single-use devices are routinely reused in low-income countries because buying new ones isn't affordable
no standard protocol exists for reprocessing these single-use devices, so authors wrote a protocol and tested it
they swabbed using breathing equipment before and after cleaning and counted the bacteria on each
they used the same CFU counting method and applied it to actual hospital equipment

sources.title: Evolution of the Global Burden of Viral Infections from Unsafe Medical Injections, 2000–2010
sources.authorsRaw: Jacques Pépin, Claire Nour Abou Chakra, Eric Pépin, Vincent Nault, Louis Valiquette
summary: tracks how many viral infections world wide comes from reusing injection equipment without sterilization
The World Health Organization's 2000 estimate balmed unsafe injections for 5% of new HIV infections, 32% of new hepatitis B infections, and 40% of new hepatitis C infections in developing countries
the estimates are made by multiplying how often equipment is reused, how common the virus already is, how likely it is to be transmitted, and how many injections people get
shows what happens when reuse is caused by scarcity and availability of tools instead of choice
sources.apaRaw: Pépin, J., Abou Chakra, C. N., Pépin, E., Nault, V., & Valiquette, L. (2014). Evolution of the global burden of viral infections from unsafe medical injections, 2000-2010. PloS one, 9(6), e99677. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0099677

sources.title: Ethical and regulatory issues in the application of 3D printing in orthopaedics: A scoping review
sources.authorsRaw: Francis Akpa-Inyang, Antoine Rocher, Megan O'Connor, Leonard Marais
summary: when a hospital prints its own 3D devices, it becomes a manurfacturer under law
this blurs the lines on who bears responsibility if a 3D printed device fails
officials haven't clearly defined rules for 3D printing in hospitals
3D printing facilities are told to follow quality standards, so if this is being done at hospitals, that puts another burden on them
sources.apaRaw: Akpa-Inyang, F., Rocher, A., O’Connor, M., & Marais, L. (2025). Ethical and regulatory issues in the application of 3D printing in orthopaedics: A scoping review. Journal of Orthopaedic Reports, 4(2), 100610. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jorep.2025.100610

sources.title: Legal issues and underexplored data protection in medical 3D printing: A scoping review
sources.authorsRaw: Ante B V Pettersson, Rosa Maria Ballardini, Marc Mimler, Phoebe Li, Mika Salmi, Timo Minssen, Ian Gibson, Antti Mäkitie
summary: reviewed 49 articles on the legal problems of 3D medical devices
found no clear answer as to who is liable when a 3D printed device that is also personalized fails
the law surrounding this is vague and doesn't cleanly separate custom-made devices from patient-matched ones
law hasn't made it clear what a design file even is, so it's not clear who's to blame if a 3D printed device fails, its also not clear who even owns the file
sources.apaRaw: Ante, Rosa Maria Ballardini, Mimler, M., Li, P., Salmi, M., Timo Minssen, Gibson, I., & Antti Mäkitie. (2023). Legal issues and underexplored data protection in medical 3D printing: A scoping review. Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology, 11. https://doi.org/10.3389/fbioe.2023.1102780

sources.title: Ethical Issues of 4D Printed Medical Devices
sources.authorsRaw: Andrés Díaz Lantada
summary: typically, manufacturer is accountable when a 4D printed device injures someone
chain of responsibility breaks down when designs are shared online and can be printed anywhere
raises concerns regarding who answers for a design someone downloaded then modified, original creator or modifier
argues that regulators (like FDA) need to find ways to track design changes and do quality control to avoid endangering people on accident

summary: a Brescia hospital ran out of ventilator valvues during the 2020 covid crisis
original parts costed thousands each and had to be swapped every 8 hours, which just wasn't feasible during a high-demand epidemic
local startup reverse-engineered the ventilator valves and printed ~100 for free (about 1 qauid in material for each valve)
founder said they had no intent to profit from or keep the design

original manufacturer apparently refused to share blueprints and warned the company that they may face a patent suit
valves were printed on site at the hospital using regular filament
this shows the 2 sides of the conflict surrounding 3D printing in medical: the patients in need on one side, and patent holders on the other

sources.title: Is 3D printing a humanitarian technology?
sources.authorsRaw: Ben Britton
summary: talks about an aid organization testing wheter 3D printing medical supplies on site is worth doing in Nepa
targetted cheap but important items: umbilical cord clams, oxygen fittings, hospital supplies
argues that the value for 3D printed items is for after disaster where supply routes are broken and areas can't get vital resources they need to survive
team ran 11 assessment visits to hospitals and health posts before investing in any equipment
Put importance on finding what people lacdk before automatically deciding that 3D printing is the answer.
